summary: Draft candidate package for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power. The clean Win25H2Clean phase-0 batch confirmed the parent key exists while the value is absent on baseline, the repo power notes carry an exact docs hit with literal 1, the targeted current-build string batch found an exact ntoskrnl.exe Unicode hit, the shared mega-trigger runtime lane armed candidate value 1 but recovered without an exact hit, and a new retained local-KD disassembly pass shows the visible generic power-setting query/store layer operating through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, and PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks rather than a visible registry API. The candidate remains research-only because the current-build live state, exact registration/binding path, and any earlier Control\Power seeding path are still unresolved in this checkout.

validation_proof.notes: The repo power notes provide the exact candidate name, literal value, and intended symbol mapping, but they do not by themselves prove current-build runtime seeding semantics.

setting.name: Allow System Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This low-level Control\Power value appears to influence whether system-required power requests are converted into execution-required behavior inside the kernel power-request subsystem.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when they want to understand how execution-required power requests are enabled, overridden, or collapsed into runtime power-request behavior.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The candidate now has enough docs, static, and debugger evidence for a real draft package, but the visible current-build power-setting query/store layer looks in-memory and callback-driven, so the decisive question is earlier seeding rather than the visible query/set code path.
setting.professional_notes: The Win25H2Clean 96-key phase-0 existence batch confirmed that HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power exists while AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests itself is absent on the clean baseline. Repo power notes document an exact literal of 1 and map the setting to PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution. The targeted string batch on the current build found an exact Unicode hit in C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe for the value name. A shared mega-trigger runtime lane then armed candidate value 1 for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests but the Procmon export recovered in an aborted state and did not yield an exact read. The new retained local-KD power-setting query/store pass disassembled PopQueryPowerSettingUlong, PopGetPowerSettingValue, and PopSetPowerSettingValue. In the retained path, the generic power-setting subsystem acquires PopSettingLock, resolves configuration objects through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, updates PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, walks PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks, and schedules PopSetNotificationWork without a visible registry API. That evidence narrows the open question: if this candidate is still registry-backed on the current build, the Control\Power seeding must occur earlier than the visible generic query/store layer.
